title: Soft launch capacity checklist and staggered rollout scenarios Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the working checklist and three staggered rollout scenarios for a customer-facing soft launch (limited cohort) across NA / EU / APAC cloud regions. Focus is on warm-pool sizing, pre-stage windows, acceptance triggers, rollback thresholds, and low-risk activation lanes to validate autoscaling, KV cache priming, and monitoring hooks before a weighted production rollout.

Background and constraints:
- We are preparing a soft launch tied to the new 1.3 model-serving stack with optimized kernels for A100/RTX-class instances.
- Budget: reserve capacity for the soft launch not to exceed a 6% incremental monthly committed spend vs current baseline.
- Latency SLO targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms for generation endpoints; error budget per region = 0.5% of requests per day.
- We must maintain isolation for Dedicated customers; soft launch only deploys to hosted clusters and dedicated staging pools.

Assumptions (baseline inputs):
- Typical token-per-request distribution: median 48 tokens, 90th percentile 256 tokens.
- Baseline utilization on production fleet: NA 68%, EU 55%, APAC 42% (pre-soft-launch).
- Warm-pool goodness: 8–12% of active fleet measured by GPU-ready instances reduces cold-start tail latency by ~40%.

Warm-pool and prestage sizing (proposal):
- NA: target warm-pool = 11% of active serving GPUs; pre-stage window = T-48h (gradual ramp to warm pool over 24h).
- EU: target warm-pool = 9%; pre-stage window = T-36h.
- APAC: target warm-pool = 14% (higher variability and expected growth); pre-stage window = T-72h (account for zone cold availability).
- Global safety buffer: +2% warm-pool reserved for cross-region failover.

Soft-launch cohorts and timelines (high-level):
- Cohort A (internal + pilot customers): week 0–2. Single NA zone, 20k qps token-equivalent, warm-pool at 11%.
- Cohort B (early-access customers): week 3–5. NA full region + EU single zone, ramp to 40% of target traffic, monitor KPIs 48h.
- Cohort C (geographic expansion): week 6–8. Add EU full region + APAC single zone, ramp to 75% of soft-launch traffic.
- Post-soft-launch evaluation: week 9: evaluate evasion triggers, cost delta, and quality regressions; decide go/no-go for progressive rollout to 100% traffic.

Rollout scenarios (three paths; choose conservative -> moderate -> aggressive):
1) Conservative path (recommended for high-reg risk customers):
   - NA first, then EU, then APAC with full 72h observation windows. Only 25% traffic increments and manual sign-off by infra on-call.
   - Rollback triggers: sustained SLA violation > 0.6% for 1 hour OR p95 latency spike > 2x baseline for 30 minutes.
   - Estimated additional GPUs required: NA +120 (gradual), EU +80, APAC +60.

2) Moderate path (default for hosted launches):
   - Parallel NA + EU staggered by 48h, APAC on week 3. Automated rollback allowed with on-call review after auto-fix attempts.
   - Rollback triggers: error budget burn >50% over 2h OR CPU/GPU thermal throttling events >2 nodes.
   - Estimated additional GPUs required: NA +90, EU +70, APAC +90 (due to longer pre-stage).

3) Aggressive path (time-sensitive marketplace launches):
   - Launch all regions in a rolling 24h window with canary traffic split (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Live circuit-breaker required.
   - Rollback triggers stricter: any certificate of unexplained degradation on p50/p95 or KV cache miss rate >12% sustained.
   - Estimated additional GPUs required: NA +200, EU +140, APAC +120. Higher cost and risk.

Operational checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Capacity reservations created with cloud providers for planned GPU types and soft-eviction policies set.
- [ ] Warm-pool autoscaler configured with target percentages per region.
- [ ] KV cache priming job scheduled to run during pre-stage windows; validate cache hit target >= 55% after 12h.
- [ ] Canary test harness: end-to-end synthetic traffic generator with real prompt templates and metrics collection (traces, token counts, cost).
- [ ] Observability: per-model latency/throughput dashboards, trace sampling at 10%, and alert thresholds set to the rollback triggers above.
- [ ] Cost smoke test: run 24h of soft-launch traffic in staging with billing meter emulation.
- [ ] Chaos scenario runbook: simulate single-zone failure, network egress throttle, and model fallback behavior.
- [ ] Security review: ensure no customer data leaks in logs for pilot tenants; audit logs enabled.

Monitoring and acceptance criteria (per-region, measured during observation windows):
- Availability >= 99.4% over 48h window.
- Actual warm-pool hit rate >= 50% within first 24h of pre-stage.
- Token-cost delta per 1k tokens <= 12% vs baseline (unless justified by performance gain).
- No more than one P1-class incident attributable to the rollout during the entire soft launch.

Rollback and mitigation playbook (quick steps):
1) Reduce traffic to canary pool (5%) and engage infra on-call.
2) If thermal/GPU errors, trigger fallback to older quantized model variant and drain affected nodes.
3) Expand warm-pool to +3% and re-run priming; if that fails, pause rollout and revert routing to pre-launch model routing.
4) Post-incident, capture root cause, patch, and run regression against the synthetic harness before resuming.

Cost and utilization modeling notes (for finance):
- Model unit: effective GPU-hours consumed by generation workload after batching and caching adjustments.
- Conservative utilization assumption for soft-launch planning: increase in active GPU-hours by 18% across NA/EU/APAC for the first 30 days.
- Suggested tagging for cost centers: soft-launch-q3-2026, warm-pool-expense, cohort-A/B/C.

Open decisions / questions:
- Should we include Dedicated pilot customers in cohort B or hold Dedicated completely out until full production? (ops/hosting input required)
- Final warm-pool percentage for APAC (14% vs 18%) — input from platform-eng on historical cold-starts.
- Approval for an additional +2% buffer cross-region (finance sign-off required if buffer triggers reserved spend increase).

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Arjun: confirm spot vs reserved mix for NA warm-pool by 2026-06-15.
- Sofia: schedule KV priming jobs and validate hit rates in staging by 2026-06-18.
- Maya (owner): finalize rollback thresholds and update monitoring dashboards by 2026-06-20.
- Liam: run cost smoke test and produce 24h report by 2026-06-21.

Next sync: weekly cadence on Fridays 10:00 PT starting 2026-06-11 (infra war room until soft-launch completion).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working checklist; feedback requested on warm-pool percentages (APAC) and suggested rollback sensitivity. If you update the doc, add your initials and date inline to help the on-call team trace changes.
